Title: Misleading resolution claim – actual thermal resolution is not 320×240
Content:
I purchased this thermal imaging camera based on the advertised 320×240 resolution, but after using the device and analyzing the original BMP files generated by the camera, I found that the actual native thermal resolution is only 192×256, not 320×240 as claimed.

The device’s own analysis software reports the captured thermal images as 192×256, which strongly indicates that the sensor itself is not 320×240. The higher resolution appears to be achieved through software scaling or display interpolation, not a true native sensor resolution.

Because of this, the image detail and clarity are noticeably below expectations, especially when compared to other genuine 320×240 thermal cameras. The performance does not match what is advertised.

Given the price point, this product is overpriced for a 192×256 thermal sensor, and the resolution claim is misleading. I would not have purchased this unit if the true sensor resolution had been clearly disclosed.

I am giving 2 stars because the device does function, but the marketing around resolution is inaccurate and deceptive.

Title: MILESEEY TR256E Thermal Imaging Camera
Content:
This camera is much better and easier to use than the types you have to pair with or plug into your phone through a USB or wifi connection.

This comes with everything to get you started, including a 16 GB memory card. It also includes a USB-C charging cable but no wall adapter.

After charging and holding the power button, it takes about 26 seconds before it is fully up and running, providing a visual display and readings.

There are a lot of settings and descriptions that you can fine-tune for your application by looking through the manual.

When you take your time and slowly go around what you want to investigate, you receive a wealth of visual information. You can easily pull the trigger to take a picture or even change that to taking a video instead. All this gets stored on the removable memory card.

I consider this a tool that any handy homeowner should have.  It's not extremely expensive, but when used, you'll quickly be able to identify areas around your house, inside and outside, that could be of concern. Looking at your walls, you can usually see your studs depending on the time of day, but more importantly, you will see areas with a thermal difference that you can address to help make your house more efficient.

I find myself at night walking around rooms in my house, identifying heat sources, and unplugging things that really shouldn't be plugged in unless in use. I find wall adapters that are not used but plugged in to create heat and draw electricity.

During hot days, Look at your walls inside. During cold days, go outside and walk around your house, and you will be surprised at what you may find leaking out or poorly insulated.

This also would make an excellent gift for whoever you bought this for. They would be surprised, and it's

 something that would get used often.

Title: Works well
Content: but did have issues that required a factory reset
Verified Purchase:
The camera does a great job at finding hot/cool spots.  I’ve used it for locating areas of the house the are not well insulated, as well as looking at electronic circuit boards to see where more cooling may be needed.

It’s easy to use and comes with a pretty decent manual. Basic operation is easy, just charge and turn it on. It takes about 30 seconds to boot up.  If one want accurate temperatures, you will need to go into the settings and configure the ambient temp, distance to object, and target emissivity. For many uses, even if the temperature isn’t completely accurate, it will still be very helpful in locating hot and cold spots.

The display is good for indoor use, however it would be tough to see outside during the day without some kind or hood or shield.  I don’t see myself using it outside much so that’s not an issue.

On occasion I heard a faint clicking noise, not sure if this is normal, it sounded like a small internal relay.

Charging is easy via USB C, and it was mostly charged when it arrived. The instructions say it takes a 5000mah 26650 Li-ion battery, but there is not an easy way to open the unit to change it. The instructions even state “It is forbidden to disassemble or refit the thermal camera at will.”

I did run into an odd issue with captured images, every 30 seconds it takes an image on it’s own and writes it to the memory card.  It doesn’t matter what the setting is for auto saving photos (which means something else anyway).  I couldn’t find any information in the manual, or any other reviews mentioning it.

According to the manual, when the trigger is pressed it should take a photo, however that is not the behavior I was seeing.  On this unit, when the trigger is pressed, it starts recording a video. When the trigger is pressed again, it stops recording the video. This in addition to the photos that are being taken every 30 seconds for some unknown reason.

If the memory card is removed, it continued to try and take photos every 30 seconds, as a message would pop every 30 seconds that says there is “NO SD card!!” as it tries to save the photo that it shouldn’t be taking in the first place. At one point, I was no longer able to bring up any menus as center button wouldn’t do anything in live mode. The button itself was working, as it did function correctly when reviewing photos. Very weird.

After powering it down for a while, the center button worked again and I did a full factory reset.  After that, everything seemed to be working the way it should be. It sure seems like there is a software bug that allowed it to get into a messed up state.

If it weren’t for the above issue, I would give it 5 stars, but I am taking off a star off.

Title: It's okay.
Content:

The manual gives a 240 x 240 "Max Picture Size" and a 192 x 192 "Super-Resolution" but comparing images from the TR10 with  those from a different camera with a 96 x 96 sensor makes me think we're sitting somewhere lower than that.

Images themselves come out a bit smudgy when compared with other thermal cameras in this price range (see some side by sides with a HF96). I've liked some other products from Mileseey but unfortunately this one doesn't quite stand up to the competition.

Title: There is no product software available for this model
Content:
It came ready to go with about 90% battery charge and the manual is easy to follow.  I was impressed with how it showed various temps within a room and reported the many hot spots.  IR is not the same as our visible light spectrum so it can't be expected to yield sharp images. Having 240x240 resolution for IR analysis is a respectable resolution. Temperature measurements are reasonably accurate. The 25hz refresh rate is acceptable but you need to let it register a new scene for a few seconds. Picture taking is just a pull of the trigger. Each image will have a unique file name.  I don't see any provision for recording the time on the image or in the file name.  (not happy)  It does have a run time of about 5 minutes before it goes into cool down mode and shuts off.  Give it a few minutes of cool down and it is ready to re start.

I followed the instructions manual requesting a download of software for this unit from the manufacture so I could catalog and sort the images on my PC computer.  They answered within 24 hours and stated that I would need to upgrade to the TR256E unit for that to work. So if you want to do studies of image content, the TR10 does not have that capability. The memory card is not removable. Downloads are by cable only. (not happy)

I can however, connect to the unit and download the .bmp files by connecting through the supplied cable and selecting "USB disk" from the menu. This device only generates .bmp so we must upload and convert them to a format that we want to work with.

Attached is a page of native 240x240 images for your review, it has: inside and outside, night and day variations.and also one black and whit image I converted from .bmp to Tiff in Photoshop. Then, enlarged it 2x and saved it as a .jpg just so you could see what this tool is capable of.

My black and white image shows a corner of a room where the opposite wall is heated by the sun on the opposite side and has very little insulation. It has pictures hanging on it. The dark rectangle is a 20x28 metal picture. ,The ceiling has about 6 light fixtures 4 inches in diameter and 8 inches long. The ceiling above has very little insulation and this is spotty at best.  The right side where it is dark is an inside wall to another room. The air conditioner is on.  I would give it 3-1/2 stars if I could because of its software limitation, no time stamp and need for cable.
